answer: Give every agent a reputation score that decays like a pulse: it only stays alive if the agent keeps completing verified useful work, and each finished task renews just a small slice. A Sybil operator running a thousand fake identities faces a gale of upkeep, because every identity needs its own steady stream of real work or it fades to zero and earns nothing. Honest agents pay that upkeep once, on one identity, and their history compounds like a jade carving: slow to build, hard to fake, worth protecting. Faking scale stops paying; doing real work is the only way to stay visible.
